# Rear door molding removal and paint restoration

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Pull rubber door moldings off, scrape and wire brush rusted areas, then apply paint and lubricate channels. [t275]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Pull the rubber door moldings off to expose hidden rust.
2. [Partial] Scrape and wire brush the area until most surface rust is gone, focusing on the top 5/6 inch of paint.

_Procedure reported by [t275]._

## Tools

- Wire brush [t275]
- [Partial] Dremel [t275]

## Tips & gotchas

- Apply a couple coats of paint after cleaning. [t275]
- [Partial] Lubricate the inside channel with dielectric grease before reattaching the molding to prevent sticking. [t275]
